chapter: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
title: Cab Calloway's 1951 big band, the Uruguay festival and the years to 1957
summary: In 1951 he played baritone in Cab's new band, which went to the festival in Uruguay and toured the States and Canada. Between 1951 and 1957 he freelanced at the Central Plaza and Metropole.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Right. Right. He was with Fletcher when they got the new band out of the Grand Terrace at first with Chu and all -- Chu and then Ben came and took Chu's place after that. Of course, Chu went with Cab. Then, '51 I went to -- Cab organized a big, new band.
Right, so we're back with Cab.

And I went with Cab. I played baritone in this band, baritone sax. And we had Hilton Jefferson on first and the fellow that used to be with the Blue Rhythm Band. I can never think of his name, on alto with Cab. He used to be with the Blue Rhythm Band, and he's from Chicago. He's been working out -- he just retired from the U.N. here late -- here recently. I can never think of that boy's name, and I knew him for years. Well, anyhow, it was Jeff, him and I was playing

baritone, had Ike Quebec on one tenor and Sam Taylor on the other tenor. Jonah Jones and Doc Cheatham and Shad Collins were the trumpets. And Butch -- I don't know his last name -- he was on one trombone, and Eddie Burke was on the other trombone.

And Milt Hinton, Panama Francis on drums, Milt Hinton on bass and Dave Rivera on piano. And we went down to Uruguay to play for the festival down there, and all of this was involved with trips. So we went down there, and we were down there about eight weeks. We stopped off in Rio, and then we went to Montevideo and stayed there for the duration at the headquarters, and then we went down to Punta del Este, and it was a very marvelous trip, had a great time down there.
Then we came back and traveled through the States again, went all through the South, and we didn't get to California, but we -- into Canada, wound up in Toronto and Montreal.
Well, according to this, you then continued to work on and off with Cab throughout the '50s when you worked in Miami and Las Vegas, et cetera.
